text:
anjali: Heads up — new Dedicated customer in eu-west behind a corporate outbound proxy. Security team asked for a single 'allowlist' artifact they can hand to their firewall/proxy team. What concrete IPs/hostnames/ports do we normally tell customers, and any gotchas (proxy auth, TLS inspection, hairpinning)?

jay: Short answer: prefer hostnames + CONNECT on 443 and DNS allowed. If they insist on IPs, give region CIDRs but warn about ephemeral egress from autoscaling pools. Typical items:
- hostnames: api.redwood-inference.com, artifacts.redwood-inference.com, registry.redwood-inference.com
- ports: 443 (TLS), 80 (optional for redirects), 53 UDP/TCP to their DNS resolver
- proxy: must support HTTP CONNECT for TLS tunnelling (proxy-auth okay if they can provide credentials)

liam: To add: our nodes pull model blobs and container images. Long-lived keepalives are important. Proxy timeouts < 60s can cause streaming/long-poll disconnects and weird client-side failures. Also if customer does SNAT per-session with port-preservation disabled we can see 5xx from origin when multiple flows reuse ports.

maria: Big gotcha: TLS inspection (corporate MITM) breaks cert validation for some components (we don't pin for all endpoints but some third-party registries do). If their proxy re-signs TLS, they need to deploy a CA that their agents trust or allow those hostnames through w/out MITM. Also SNI rewrite breaks virtual-hosted endpoints => allow real hostnames via CONNECT.

anjali: They said they do proxy-chaining (internal -> outbound edge proxy) and perform authentication at the edge. Any header/behavior we need to support?

jay: We can work with standard Proxy-Authorization Basic/Bearer headers. If they do NTLM/Kerberos it's trickier; NTLM breaks connection reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing. Recommend they use basic/token auth on the outbound proxy or let our nodes talk directly.

liam: If proxy modifies Host/SNI, DNS-based service discovery will fail for some backends. We saw a customer last quarter where SNI rewrite caused requests to land on wrong ALBs. Debug tip: reproduce with `openssl s_client -connect artifacts.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername artifacts.redwood-inference.com` from a node behind their proxy (or use `curl --proxy`).

maria: Debug commands that help when they report failures: 
```
# test HTTP CONNECT through their proxy
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.addr:8080 --proxy-user user:pass https://artifacts.redwood-inference.com/health
# check SNI from client side
openssl s_client -connect proxy.addr:8080 -servername artifacts.redwood-inference.com
```
(share redacted output with us, don't paste creds)

devops-bot: deploy/edge-pull failed: 407 Proxy Authentication Required (artifact fetch).

scott-oncall-bot: recent incident snippet: 
```
2025-08-12T09:12:43Z node-23 fetch artifacts.redwood-inference.com 407 Proxy Authentication Required
2025-08-12T09:12:43Z node-23 retry 1/3
2025-08-12T09:12:47Z node-23 fetch artifacts.redwood-inference.com 200 OK
```

anjali: Two customer-specific asks: 1) they want minimal list we can guarantee for Dedicated in region eu-west; 2) they asked if we can support a static outbound IP as an alternative.

liam: For (1) we can provide a compact artifact: canonical hostnames + region CIDR that covers our autoscaling NAT pool (note: CIDR may change when we scale; we publish a weekly file and a webhook). If they demand absolute stability, it's not safe unless they allow hostnames or accept a larger CIDR. For (2) yes — Dedicated can be configured with static NAT egress per customer (recommended for strict allowlists).

maria: Also mention ports for healthchecks: allow outbound 443 and ephemeral ports for streaming. If they run an outbound proxy on non-standard ports, call that out. And ask if they have TLS inspection — if yes, they'll need to trust our CA for any re-signed certs.

jay: Quick checklist to send them (one-liner each):
- Allow CONNECT/TLS to api.redwood-inference.com, artifacts.redwood-inference.com, registry.redwood-inference.com on 443
- Permit DNS (53 UDP/TCP) to their resolvers and outbound to our hostnames
- If using proxy auth, provide credentials or allow unauthenticated egress to our hostnames for the node subnet
- Do not rewrite SNI or Host headers for our endpoints
- If TLS inspection is unavoidable, they must install a trusted CA we can validate against or enable static egress IPs

anjali: I'll draft that and send to the customer sec team. Anything else we should include in the doc?

maria: Add an optional troubleshooting snippet for packet capture and where to look for 407 vs 522 (connect timeout) vs 503 (upstream). And note the weekly CIDR feed + webhook.

anjali: Perfect. I'll post the draft and ping @jay and @liam for review before sending. :thumbsup:
